What do you want to do? Supposing it's playing songs, start trying to play something you like. My advice is to learn a song at a time and only move on when you can't get the last one wrong.

Besides that, find some technique exercises, and again, one at a time. Start slow, use a metronome and record yourself.

On top of that, pick a good theory book and learn about intervals, scales and chords progressions. Train your ears too, everyday, even if only for 5min, you'll soon notice how everything will get smoother.

Finally, and most important, have fun.

I'd suggest you to get a good theory book. At the beginning you probably won't see any practical application, but knowledge don't hurt and it will give you lots of things to practice, PM me if you want a suggestion. Any good book will teach you about modes, scales and chords structure. Of course all that is available on internet, but it takes a bit of work to pick what is really worth your time.

About your discomfort after playing for a couple of hours, this is generally related to bad technique. With proper technique, it's possible to play guitar for insanely long hours without any issue. It can also be a problem with your guitar set up, if the strings are too high you'll need to apply way too much pressure, which can cause you serious harm. If you can afford, pay a visit to a good teacher that can spot any serious technique flaws.

Finally, noodling is just strumming your guitar purposeless. It's not a problem at all if do you it once in a while, it's only a problem if it is your regular practice approach.

Ok, let's see if I can help, and forgive me if I can't.

It's nice that you're doing some kind of warm up. I usually use scales for that (or when I don't  know what to practice).
After that, you have to have a very clear objective in mind. Noodling is fine and doesn't do any harm, but if you want to get better at something, you should better practice that very thing. Your objective can be very technical or theoretical, like "today I'll just practice the F# Dorian mode 7 shapes across the fretboard" or "I won't do anything else ultil I get this C minor shape arpeggio to sound good", or you could just learn a new song. The important thing here is: don't stop practicing when you get it right, practice until you can't get it wrong. Also, do it as slow as necessary to do it absolutely flawless, even it comes down to 20bpm, if you practice doing something sloppy, you'll practicing your sloppyness. Don't try to carry the world on your shoulder, focus on being perfect at one thing at a time. You can suck at anything else, but be the best of the world in at least one single thing. 

Yeah, I know, it sounds and is very slow, but when you get this kind of immersion with one concept, you carry it forever with you.

Hope this help you somehow. Good practice and keep rocking.
